restatement: Expose the headless template core over a dependency-free node http server: POST /v1/render, /v1/validate, /v1/analyze and GET /v1/spec return the documented result bodies (template problems are 200 with ok false and located diagnostics), GET /v1/openapi.json serves the committed OpenAPI 3.1 document byte for byte and that document matches the router table, malformed or hostile requests get JSON 400/404/405/413/415 errors without crashing, request limits can only lower the server's limits, and an end-to-end test drives every route on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port and closes it.
verification_plan: Check each route handler returns the documented body: RenderResult for render, {ok, diagnostics} for validate, analysis with required and blocks for analyze, spec() for spec; a template error yields 200, ok false, empty output and located diagnostics first.

Check request validation: bad JSON, non-object body, missing or non-string template, non-object data (including null and arrays), non-object options, non-boolean strictMode, non-object or bad-typed limits all give 400 invalid-request with {error:{code,message}} only.

Check 404 for unknown paths, 405 with an Allow header for known paths with the wrong method, 413 via Content-Length and streamed size, 415 for non-JSON POST content types while accepting a charset parameter; every response has a JSON content type.
Check hostile bodies (oversized, wrong type, wrong content type, engine exceptions) produce a JSON reply and never an unhandled rejection or thrown error in the request handler.
Check limit merging takes min(request, server) per key and that omitted keys keep the server value.
Check GET /v1/openapi.json bytes equal api/openapi.json on disk on every platform, the document is 3.1, its paths and methods equal the routes table, and its schemas match what core actually returns.
Check the e2e test binds 127.0.0.1 port 0, uses node's http client for all five routes, and closes the server; check afterEach stops servers in the unit tests.
Check no runtime dependency is added and the default listen host is 127.0.0.1.
Check earlier findings f1 (CRLF byte equality) and f2 (null data/options) are fixed, and the frozen test change is only added table rows.

findings.title: After a 413 or 415 the server reads and discards the whole remaining body before replying, with no cap

serves.scenario: A client that declares or streams a body far over maxBodyBytes (or an endless chunked body, or a huge text/plain body) keeps the connection and the server's read loop busy until it stops sending or node's requestTimeout fires; the process does not crash and memory is not retained, so the goal-critical question is still answered adequately, but request limits do not bound the work spent on a rejected request.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: Start createServer({maxBodyBytes: 64}); send POST /v1/render with content-type application/json, Transfer-Encoding chunked, and keep writing chunks; no 413 arrives until the client ends the body (sendError waits for req 'end' after req.resume()).

evidence: test:oa-doc: GET /v1/openapi.json serves api/openapi.json byte for byte
